messages:
Alex: Found a reproducible OOM in the Android sample app after rotating the device while a token refresh occurred. Repro: login -> rotate -> call /user/profile -> crash.

Maria: Oh no. Which okhttp/retrofit versions and can you paste stacktrace + interceptor?

Alex: okhttp 4.11.0, retrofit 2.9.0. Trimmed stack:
FATAL EXCEPTION: main
java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Failed to allocate...
Caused by: java.lang.IllegalStateException: Activity leaked: com.example.sample.MainActivity@3f2a5c7
  at com.example.sample.AuthInterceptor.intercept(AuthInterceptor.kt:34)

Alex: Simplified interceptor: class AuthInterceptor(private val tokenProvider: TokenProvider): Interceptor { override fun intercept(chain: Interceptor.Chain): Response { val req = chain.request(); val token = tokenProvider.token; val withAuth = req.newBuilder().header("Authorization","Bearer $token").build(); val resp = chain.proceed(withAuth); if (resp.code == 401) { synchronized(this){ tokenProvider.refreshIfNeeded() }; val retryReq = withAuth.newBuilder().header("Authorization","Bearer ${tokenProvider.token}").build(); return chain.proceed(retryReq) } return resp }}

Alex: TokenProvider was created in MainActivity and holds an Activity reference for showing login dialog — interceptor indirectly kept Activity alive during request -> rotation causes leak -> OOM after repeated rotations.

Kevin: That pattern is classic. Never capture Activity in a network singleton. TokenProvider should use Application context and publish UI events. Also prefer OkHttp Authenticator for 401 flows.

Maria: Quick fixes: 1) move UI out of TokenProvider; use ApplicationContext + LiveData/event bus. 2) Replace manual retry with an Authenticator (designed for credential refresh).

Jordan: Also ensure you don't reuse/consume response bodies before retrying. And set okHttpClient.retryOnConnectionFailure(false) in debug builds to simplify repro.

Alex: Switched TokenProvider to app-scoped TokenStore, moved dialog trigger to observed event, and implemented TokenAuthenticator: class TokenAuthenticator(private val tokenStore: TokenStore): Authenticator { override fun authenticate(route: Route?, response: Response): Request? { if (responseCount(response) >= 2) return null; val newToken = tokenStore.refreshBlocking() ?: return null; return response.request.newBuilder().header("Authorization","Bearer $newToken").build() } private fun responseCount(response: Response): Int { var res: Response? = response; var result = 1; while (res?.priorResponse != null) { result++; res = res.priorResponse } return result }}

Lina: Authenticator avoids holding Activity state on the network path. responseCount guard prevents retry storms.

CI-Bot: Sampleapp CI flagged a flake on Firebase Test Lab for leaked Activity after rotation. See: https://ci.redwood/xyz/12345

Kevin: Let's add a short note in devex onboarding: "Do not retain Activity/Fragment references in networking singletons; use Application context; prefer Authenticator for token refresh; cap retries." Many sample apps repeat this mistake.

Alex: I'll open a PR to update sample repo + SDK README. Changes: TokenStore app-scoped, switch to Authenticator, set retryOnConnectionFailure(false) in debug, add unit test simulating rotation by nulling activity ref.

Maria: I can review and add a small Robolectric e2e to check no activity references remain. :thumbsup:

Jordan: Also consider adding a lint rule or checklist: "networking objects must not retain Activity/Fragment references." Low effort, high ROI.

Alex: Will add issue to devex backlog.

Lina: Great catch 389 this'll save teams headaches.
